answer: Quadratic staking + time-locks: each identity locks ripple tokens; required stake grows quadratically per added identity from the same source. N fake IDs cost O(N^2), not O(N), making mass Sybil creation prohibitively expensive. Stakes release over epochs, preventing instant burn-and-recreate. On-chain attestations verify signed commitments against the staking contract before voting power is assigned. lotus seeds challenge randomization; willow sets slashing for double-signing. Cost rises super-linearly with attack scale; honest users pay a modest linear fee. Sybil attacks are uneconomic.
